issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface, but the solution implementation uses a different interface name (Mountable) for the rideable behavior. Additionally, the solution contains an empty Rideable.java file. This naming/type mismatch between solution and specification/template can confuse students (which interface to implement) and cause incompatibilities with expected code/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface naming across artifacts. Either (a) rename Mountable in the solution to Rideable and update Pig/Seal to implement Rideable (and remove the empty Rideable.java), or (b) update the problem statement and template to use Mountable consistently. Ensure a single interface name (Rideable) is present and implemented by the rideable animals.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable', but the solution implementation uses an interface named 'Mountable' (and leaves Rideable.java empty). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual interface (providing messageOnRide()) creates a mapping barrier: students expect to implement/use Rideable as described, but the solution's classes implement Mountable instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (update Mountable.java -> Rideable.java and have Pig/Seal implement Rideable), and remove or populate the empty Rideable.java; or (B) update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' everywhere. This alignment ensures students can directly map the problem description to the provided code.
